How to Write a Chef Resume

A chef resume should identify cuisine, service format, covers, station or kitchen leadership, menu development, food cost, safety, and quality. The scale and style of the operation should be immediately clear.

Example

Chef resume summary

Use this as a pattern for level, scope, specialty, and evidence. Do not copy facts that are not yours.

Chef with 10 years of experience in high-volume contemporary restaurants and hotel banquets. Led a twelve-person brigade, delivered services of up to 450 covers, and reduced food cost through menu and purchasing changes.
Recommended order

How to structure the resume

  1. Contact details and target title. Use the normal title from the job posting and provide working contact links.
  2. Focused summary. Establish your level, setting, specialty, and one representative outcome.
  3. Recent relevant experience. Use reverse chronological order and give the most space to work that resembles the target role.
  4. Role-specific skills. Keep a scannable list, then prove the important skills in bullets.
  5. Education and credentials. List culinary education, food-manager certification, allergen training, responsible-service credentials, and apprenticeships when current. A portfolio can support specialized pastry or presentation work.
Use only what you can support

Skills to include

Match the employer's terminology when it accurately describes your experience.

  • Menu development
  • Kitchen leadership
  • Food preparation
  • Cost control
  • Purchasing
  • Food safety
  • Inventory
  • Training
Evidence ideas

Useful metrics for a chef resume

Numbers should clarify scope or change. They do not need to be revenue figures.

Service

Covers, events, stations, or outlets supported

Cost

Food cost, waste, yield, or purchasing savings

People

Brigade size, training, retention, or promotion

Writing patterns

Chef resume bullet examples

Adapt the action, context, and result to your own verified work.

  • Led a twelve-person brigade through services of up to 450 covers.
  • Reduced food cost by 2.8 percentage points through menu and purchasing changes.
  • Created seasonal dishes using local suppliers and documented consistent yields.
  • Raised food-safety audit performance through station checks and coaching.
Look for

Strong signals

  • Culinary standard
  • Service execution
  • Cost control
  • Team leadership
Avoid

Common mistakes

  • A dish list with no kitchen or service context
  • Calling recipes proprietary in place of evidence
  • No cost, sanitation, or leadership information
  • Using awards that cannot be verified

Questions, answered

Resume FAQ

What should a chef resume include?

Lead with culinary standard, show relevant menu development experience in context, and use achievement bullets that explain scope and outcome.

What skills belong on a chef resume?

Prioritize skills from the target job that you can prove in experience, projects, education, or credentials. Useful examples include menu development, kitchen leadership, food preparation, cost control.

Can I use the example numbers and bullet points?

No. The examples demonstrate structure and specificity. Replace every action, number, tool, and result with evidence that is true for your own work.

Which resume format should I use?

Reverse chronological format works for most candidates. Use a combination format when projects or transferable skills need more emphasis, but keep dates and work history clear.
